corrections.why: 15.2 m is 50 feet, the height in the May 1930 plan for a 50-foot tower. The completed tower was 30 feet, per firelookout.com and the November 1930 report

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The September 1930 report puts the peak about five miles southeast of Bonita. The survey datasheet puts it 5.0 miles west-southwest of the Bonita Ranger Station, and 4.5 miles south of Clinton, which fits the May 1930 report that the site was directly south of Clinton. Not reconciled on the Bonita bearing.
Firelookout.com calls it a 30-foot pole L-4 tower; the 1930 reports describe a 30-foot wooden tower with a glass cabin. Both agree on 30 feet.
Firelookout.com says a platform in three trees came first, in the 1920s. The 1930 reports call the new station the twelfth on the forest. Not reconciled.

notes_for_editor: Height correction proposed: the brief's 15.2 m matches the May 1930 plan, not the built tower. A photo may exist: Montana History Portal item 20368, 'Iris fire lookout, Bonita District' (University of Montana Mansfield Library, USFS Region One collection), rights statement 'NO COPYRIGHT - UNITED STATES', dated 1930 on the page, showing the lookout before the new one was built. The image URL was not confirmed, so no photo entry was added. The survey datasheet's route description is dated 1957 and may be out of date.
